title: Glass Beach – Fort Bragg, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Glass Beach, Fort Bragg, California
excerpt: A charter bus to Glass Beach in Fort Bragg makes a long Mendocino coast drive easy. What to expect, why you cannot take the glass, and which vehicle fits.

heroImage.alt: Wave-polished sea glass covering the shingle at Glass Beach in Fort Bragg, California

extraImage.alt: The rocky Mendocino coastline north of Fort Bragg with surf breaking against low cliffs

body.text: For sixty years Fort Bragg tipped its trash over the cliff into the Pacific. The ocean spent the following decades grinding the bottles and crockery into smooth, frosted pebbles, and what was left is a shoreline that glitters. Glass Beach is a genuinely strange place — part natural wonder, part accidental monument to a bad idea — and a charter bus to Glass Beach turns a three-and-a-half-hour drive from the Bay Area into the easy part of the day.
The one rule everybody needs to hear first

You cannot take the glass. The beach is part of MacKerricher State Park, removing anything from a state park is prohibited, and after decades of visitors pocketing handfuls the supply is visibly thinner than it was. Tell your group before they get off the bus rather than after, because it is a genuinely disappointing thing to learn while holding a pocketful.

It also sets the right expectation. Groups who arrive expecting to collect souvenirs come away flat; groups who arrive to see the phenomenon come away impressed. The difference is entirely in the briefing.
What the visit is actually like

The main beach is reached from the parking area at the end of Elm Street, down a short trail. It is not a long walk, but the beach itself is rocky, uneven and reached by a scramble in places — this is not a stop where a wheelchair or an unsteady walker will get down to the glass. Plan for part of the group to stay on the bluff, where the coastal view is excellent in its own right.

Allow an hour. Low tide reveals substantially more than high tide does, and the glass photographs best when it is wet, so check a tide table when you set the arrival time. It is the single easiest way to improve the visit and it costs nothing.
What else to do while you are up there

items: The Skunk Train from downtown Fort Bragg, a historic railroad that runs inland through redwood canyon. A strong two hours and a good pairing with a short beach visit.
Mendocino village, ten minutes south: a clifftop town of restored Victorians that looks like a New England fishing port and is the best lunch stop on this coast.

The Mendocino Coast Botanical Gardens, between the two, with paths running from formal beds down to the ocean bluff. Level walking, and the accessible option if part of your group cannot manage the beach.
Point Cabrillo Light Station, a restored 1909 lighthouse on a headland with a short level approach from the parking area.

body.text: Which charter bus suits the trip

The drive matters more than the destination here. Highway 1 north of Jenner is a slow, winding coastal road, and the inland route via Highway 101 and Willits is longer in miles but usually faster and considerably easier on a large vehicle.

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/motor-coaches) is comfortable for the long haul and should take the inland route. The on-board restroom is worth real money on this drive.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) can handle the coastal highway if the scenic route is the point of the day, and parks more easily in Fort Bragg and Mendocino.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) suits a small group and goes anywhere on this coast.

body.text: From San Francisco allow three and a half to four hours by the inland route and closer to five if you take Highway 1 the whole way. From [Santa Rosa](/locations/california/santa-rosa) it is about two and a half hours, and from [Ukiah](/locations/california/ukiah) around an hour and a half over Highway 20 — which is why groups that can stage overnight inland get a far better day than those driving up and back from the Bay Area.

Anyone searching for charter bus rental near me for a Mendocino coast trip should be honest with themselves about the distance. As a single day from San Francisco it is eight hours of driving for two hours on the coast. As an overnight it is one of the best trips in Northern California. We run pickups from [Fort Bragg](/locations/california/fort-bragg), [Santa Rosa](/locations/california/santa-rosa) and [San Francisco](/locations/california/san-francisco).

September and October are the clearest months on this coast, with the least fog and the warmest days. Summer brings persistent morning fog that often does not lift until afternoon, which is atmospheric but limits the view. Winter is dramatic, wet and quiet, and storm surge can make the beach access genuinely unwise — check conditions before traveling.
